newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - July 31.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - July 31.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing,
Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:
NEW YORK - Jean maker Levi Strauss & Co. unveils what it
says is the largest campaign in the brand's history, featuring
television spots that aim squarely at the "originality and
youthfulness" of the target 18- to 22-year-old consumer. The
commercials were created by Foote Cone & Belding of San
Francisco, a unit of True North Communications.
PARIS - Perrier-Vittel, the French mineral water unit of
Swiss food and drink group Nestle, says its first foray into the
soft drinks market will target the important youth segment.
Their new drink "Fu", made from Perrier mineral water, sugar and
secret natural plant extracts, launches in France and Belgium
with a national poster campaign run by Publicis SA unit Loeb et
Associes.
NEW YORK - General Motors Corp, NBC Inc and the U.S.
Olympic Committee say the automaker has agreed to a landmark
media and sponsorship agreement. A GM official says the value of
the deal could be close to $1 billion. The pact designates GM as
the official domestic car and truck of the U.S. Olympic team and
runs through the 2008.
LONDON - Saatchi & Saatchi says it will launch a six million
pound ($9.8 million) advertising campaign for Carlsberg lager
designed to position the beer as a more contemporary brand.
GOLDEN, Colorado - Across Media Networks says it has
received a contract to create ads for a division of TCI Media
Services, the advertising arm for Tele-Communications Inc.
DALLAS - Video rental and music store operator Blockbuster
names Jim Notarnicola as executive vice president of marketing
and administration. Notarnicola has 18 years experience in
retailing and previously worked at Southland Corp, Blockbuster
says.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:
LONDON - The British government refers Capital Radio Plc's
planned 64.7 million pound acquisition of Richard Branson's
Virgin Radio to regulators, citing competition concerns. Nigel
Griffiths, minister for Competition and Consumer Affairs, says
he referred the deal to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission
due to worries about competition in London's radio advertising
market.
BRUSSELS - The European Union must gear up to profit from
the explosion of film and television services that will be
offered to consumers over the next decade, says the European
Commission. The EU executive, indirectly calling on Europe's
industry to battle U.S. dominance, says in a policy paper that
the EU's audiovisual market is set to grow 70 percent in the
next 10 years.
SINGAPORE - Singapore's Internet users will be able to
access multimedia services using broadcast links to cable
television, say officials of MediaManager, the operator of the
service. The first interactive broadcast service allows users to
receive multimedia sound and images at higher speeds via
television antennas rather than traditional dial-up phones.
FRANKFURT - New German Internet legislation set to take
effect this week will not create new limits on the development
of advertising or shopping in cyberspace, marketing experts say.
The new law sets new standards for child protection on the
Internet and defines which activities require regulation and
which can be operated without any formal licence or regulatory
oversight.
BEIJING - A Chinese scientific institute will launch a
national computer service supplying scientific and technological
information over the Internet, officials say. Wanfang Data Corp,
the commercial identity of the Institute of Scientific and
Technology Information of China, will provide information on
scientific and technological developments in China, a company
official says.
BOGOTA - Colombia's constitutional court upholds a new law
to shake up television programming but eliminates a clause that
critics said was tantamount to censorship of news shows. The
court rules program-makers will not have their contracts
automatically renewed and will have to submit fresh bids for
broadcast slots on the country's two government-controlled
channels.
BUENOS AIRES - Argentina's CEI Citicorp Holdings SA has paid
$200 million for 40 percent of media holding Grupo Federal de
Comunicaciones, says a report in El Cronista newspaper. The
group comprises television channel Telefe, Radio Continental and
publisher Editorial Atlantida. The acquisition price will not
include the group's assets, valued at $100 million.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:
BOGOTA - Fast-food chain McDonald's Corp is drawing up plans
to supply all its restaurants worldwide with Colombian coffee.
"This is a plan we're working on in conjunction with Colombia's
National Coffee Growers' Federation," says Andres Munoz, head of
marketing for McDonald's Colombian operations. The McDonald's
network in the U.S. uses about 15,500 tonnes of coffee per year,
with a similar amount used in its outlets in the rest of the
world.
MILAN - Italy's cabinet agrees to extend the nation's car
buying incentive scheme for a further 10 months, but it scales
back payments and moves to encourage the buying of more
environmentally friendly cars. Under Italy's original scheme,
introduced at the beginning of the year to run to end-September,
owners of cars more than 10 years old could trade them in for
scrapping in exchange for price discounts on new car purchases.
COSTA MESA, California - Canon Computer Systems Inc, a
subsidiary of Canon Inc, says it reduced the prices of two of
its PowerShot digital cameras. The PowerShot 600 will sell for
an estimated street price of $699 and Canon's PowerShot 350 will
sell for an estimated street price of $599.
TAIPEI - Food giant President Enterprise Corp says it will
invest at least T$10 billion ($352.1 million) to establish a
holding firm. "Investment in high-technology and large shopping
malls will be the priority of the holding firm's work area," a
company spokeswoman says.
MADRID - Volkswagen AG's Spanish unit Seat says it will keep
its factory open this year in August, making 27,000 cars in a
month it usually closes down for summer holidays.
HOUSTON - Compaq Computer Corp says it unveiled a new Armada
7300 line of mobile notebook computers. The Armada 7300 models
should be available in August, the company says, at prices
ranging from $4,399 to $4,899.
CONSUMER TRENDS:
BEIJING - Foreign breweries hoping to stake their claim to a
share of the world's largest beer market set up promotional
stands at the opening night of the Beijing International Beer
Festival. Foreign breweries are battling to stake their claim to
a share of China's army of drinkers who consumed 155 million
hectolitres of beer in 1994 and are expected to drink 220
million hectolitres in 2000.
WELLINGTON - Golden beaches, lush native bush, gushing
rivers and snow-laden mountains -- it's a package
that draws over a million tourists to New Zealand every year.
But beneath the "clean, green" image hides a tourism industry in
disarray. New Zealand's single largest foreign currency earner
is in a trough, low-level corruption is rife and tourism
operators say they're struggling to stay afloat as competition
for the holiday-maker's dollar intensifies worldwide.
